meta.title: Tajik (забони тоҷикӣ) Language Ontology
meta.description: A comprehensive ontology of the Tajik language (ISO 639-3: tgk), a Southwestern Iranian language of the Indo-European family. Tajik is the official language of Tajikistan and is closely related to Persian (Farsi) and Dari. This ontology follows the GOLD OntoLing structure, populated with data from standard pedagogical and descriptive sources.
sources: Ido, S. (2005). Tajik (Languages of the World/Materials 442). LINCOM Europa.
Perry, J. R. (2005). A Tajik Persian Reference Grammar. Brill.
Khojayori, N. & Thompson, M. (2009). Tajiki Reference Grammar for Beginners. Georgetown University Press.
Ido, S. & Mahmoodi-Bakhtiari, B. (Eds.). (2023). Tajik Linguistics. De Gruyter Mouton.
Rahimī, M. V. & Uspenskaya, L. V. (Eds.). (1954). Луғати тоҷикӣ-русӣ. Москва.
Windfuhr, G. (Ed.). (2009). The Iranian Languages. Routledge.
Lazard, G. (1992). A Grammar of Contemporary Persian. Mazda Publishers.
meta.classification: Indo-European, Indo-Iranian, Iranian, Western Iranian, Southwestern Iranian, Persian, Tajik
meta.speaker_population: Approximately 8-10 million in Tajikistan, plus significant communities in Uzbekistan (Samarkand, Bukhara), Afghanistan, Russia, Kazakhstan, and Kyrgyzstan.
meta.location: Tajikistan (official language), Uzbekistan, Afghanistan, Kyrgyzstan, Kazakhstan, and diaspora communities.
dialects: Northern dialects (based on Dushanbe, Khujand, and the Ferghana Valley)
Southern dialects (including Samarkand and Bukhara dialects)
Mountain dialects (Pamir region, which are sometimes considered separate languages)
meta.standard_dialect: Based on the northern dialects, primarily the speech of Dushanbe and its surrounding regions.

Language.definition: Tajik (забони тоҷикӣ) is a Southwestern Iranian language belonging to the Indo-European family. It is the official language of the Republic of Tajikistan and is a member of the Persian language continuum, closely related to Farsi and Dari. Tajik is characterized by a SOV word order, agglutinative-fusional morphology, the absence of grammatical gender, and a complex verb system with a notable ergative construction in the past tense of transitive verbs.
key_properties: Agglutinative-fusional morphology (extensive use of suffixes for inflection and derivation)
Absence of articles (definiteness is implied through context and the direct object marker)
Ergative construction in the past tense of transitive verbs
Izafet construction for modification and possession
Postpositional language (uses postpositions, though some prepositions exist)
Uses a modified Cyrillic alphabet (35 letters: 6 vowels and 29 consonants)
Rich system of verbal tenses, aspects, and moods

arabic_script.description: Tajik used a modified Arabic alphabet (Perso-Arabic script) from the 8th century until the 1920s. This script was adapted to represent the specific phonemes of Tajik, including the addition of letters for sounds not present in Arabic (e.g., ч, ҷ, ғ, қ, ш, ӣ).

latin_script.description: In 1928, the Latin alphabet was adopted as part of the Soviet Union's campaign of latinization. This alphabet was based on the Common Turkic Alphabet and was used for a short period before the Cyrillic script was introduced.

cyrillic_script.description: A modified Cyrillic alphabet became the official Tajik alphabet in 1940 and remains in use today. It consists of 35 letters and is adapted to represent the phonological system of Tajik.

Lexicon.definition: The inventory of sign units in Tajik, including native Iranian roots and a significant number of loanwords from Arabic, Persian, Russian, Uzbek, and other languages.

Grammar.definition: The set of rules for operating on these units, encompassing phonology, morphology, and syntax.

Language.definition: The abstract linguistic system in the minds of speakers, representing the standardized rules and vocabulary of Tajik.
Language.details: The standardized literary language of Tajikistan, based on the northern dialects and used in government, education, and media.

Speech.definition: The concrete realization of language in communication.
Speech.details: Includes dialectal variations (northern, southern, mountain), colloquial speech, and sociolects, which may differ significantly from the literary standard.

Linguistic_System.definition: Tajik is characterized by a hierarchical arrangement of units on inter-related levels: phonology, morphology, syntax, and semantics. It is a 'system of systems' where each level has its own units and rules.
Linguistic_System.system_of_systems: Tajik can be described as a 'system of systems' with hierarchically ordered levels: phonology, morphology, syntax, and semantics.

Linguistic_Taxon.definition: Tajik is a member of the Western Iranian branch of the Indo-European language family.

Taxon.definition: Tajik belongs to the Iranian language family, which is a branch of the larger Indo-European family.

Genetic_Taxon.definition: Tajik is a Southwestern Iranian language, closely related to Persian (Farsi) and Dari.
Genetic_Taxon.genetic_notes: Tajik, Farsi, and Dari descend from the same Middle Persian (Pahlavi) language and are often considered a single pluricentric language. The separation of Tajik as a distinct standard began in the 20th century during the Soviet era.

Context_of_Use_Taxon.definition: Tajik is used in a variety of contexts, including official, educational, literary, and daily communication.
konabere_contexts: Official: Used as the state language of the Republic of Tajikistan.
Literary/Standard: Based on the northern dialects, used in government, media, and literature.
Daily communication: Used by all generations in all domains of life.
Religious: Used in religious contexts, although Arabic is also significant for Islamic texts.
Oral tradition: Rich folklore and literary tradition, including the poetry of Rumi, Rudaki, and Sadriddin Ayni.

Geographic_Taxon.definition: Tajik is spoken primarily in the Republic of Tajikistan, as well as in parts of Uzbekistan, Afghanistan, Kyrgyzstan, Kazakhstan, and Russia.
Geographic_Taxon.area: Republic of Tajikistan: 143,100 km². Significant speaker populations in Samarkand and Bukhara (Uzbekistan) and in northern Afghanistan.

Political_Taxon.definition: Tajik is the official language of the Republic of Tajikistan and a recognized minority language in Uzbekistan.
Political_Taxon.konabere_political_status: Official language of the Republic of Tajikistan. Recognized as a minority language in Uzbekistan. The standard dialect is based on the northern dialects, particularly the speech of Dushanbe.

Endangerment_Taxon.definition: Tajik is not considered endangered. It is the official language of a sovereign state with a large and growing speaker population.
vitality_factors: Speaker population: ~8-10 million (Tajikistan) + significant communities in other countries
Official status: Official language of the Republic of Tajikistan
Documentation: Extensive literature, textbooks, dictionaries, and media.
Literacy programs: Highly developed educational system in Tajik.

Language_Family.definition: Tajik is a member of the Iranian language family, which is a branch of the Indo-European family.

Language_Stock.definition: Tajik is part of the Indo-European language family.

Language_Subfamily.definition: Tajik is a member of the Southwestern Iranian subfamily of Iranian languages, which also includes Persian (Farsi), Dari, and Luri.

Isolate.definition: Tajik is not an isolate; it has numerous close relatives within the Iranian and Indo-European families.

Dialect.definition: Tajik has a number of regional dialects, broadly classified into northern, southern, and mountain groups.

dialects.name: Northern Dialects
dialects.location: Dushanbe, Khujand, and the Ferghana Valley
phonological_features: Pronunciation of 'a' as a low back vowel [ɑ]

dialects.name: Southern Dialects (Samarkand-Bukhara)
phonological_features: Fronting of 'a' to 'e' in some contexts: сар → сер 'head'
Pronunciation of 'q' as [χ] in some positions: бозор → бозох 'bazaar'
Influence of Uzbek phonology (vowel harmony, consonant assimilation)
morphological_features: Use of the plural suffix -лар (from Uzbek)
Use of the Turkic izafet construction
More frequent use of Uzbek loanwords

dialects.name: Mountain Dialects
dialects.notes: Often considered separate languages (e.g., Shughni, Rushani). They are not mutually intelligible with standard Tajik.

dialects.name: Badakhshan Dialects
dialects.notes: Includes a variety of Pamir languages, which are distinct from Tajik.

Dialect.standard_dialect: The literary standard is primarily based on the northern dialects, specifically the speech of Dushanbe.

The_Linguistic_Sign.definition: Tajik linguistic signs connect a signifier (phonological form) with a signified (meaning).

Signifier.definition: The external form, which can be spoken or written.
Signifier.konabere_details: Tajik uses a modified Cyrillic alphabet of 35 letters. The spoken form is based on a system of 6 vowel and 24 consonant phonemes, with dynamic stress.

Signified.konabere_details: Lexical meaning (e.g., хона 'house', китоб 'book', хондан 'to read') and grammatical meaning (e.g., plural -ҳо, past tense -д).

Arbitrariness.definition: Predominantly arbitrary, but with some onomatopoeic elements.
Arbitrariness.konabere_details: Most words are arbitrary, though some words like 'ширхор' (to hiss) or 'ғуруз' (rumble) are onomatopoeic.

Linear_Character.definition: Elements follow one another in time.
Linear_Character.konabere_details: SOV word order; suffixes are added linearly to roots.

Double_Articulation.definition: Signs are composed of smaller meaningful signs (morphemes) and non-meaningful units (phonemes).

The_Linguistic_Sign.examples: Words and morphemes: китоб 'book', -ҳо 'plural', навиштан 'to write', -анд 'third person plural ending'.

Linguistic_Unit.definition: Linguistic units in Tajik are organized hierarchically.

Form_Unit.definition: The sensorily perceptible aspect of the sign, i.e., its spoken or written form.

Grammar_Unit.definition: The structural component of the sign, including morphemes and syntactic words.

Semantic_Unit.definition: The meaning component of the sign.

semantic_units.definition: Plural number (-ҳо), past tense (-д), definite direct object marker (-ро), genitive relationship (изофа).

Linguistic_Expression.definition: The physical representation of a linguistic unit.

expressions.Spoken: The spoken form of Tajik, produced by the vocal apparatus.
expressions.Written: The written form, using the modern Cyrillic-based alphabet (since 1940) or, historically, the Latin and Arabic scripts.

Spoken_Linguistic_Expression.definition: The physical sound form of Tajik, including dialectal variations and fast-speech processes.
Spoken_Linguistic_Expression.notes: Fast speech often involves vowel reduction (e.g., 'меравам' → 'мерам') and assimilation of consonants.

Written_Linguistic_Expression.definition: The written form of Tajik, primarily using the Cyrillic-based alphabet (35 letters) adopted in 1940. The Latin and Arabic scripts were used in earlier periods.
Written_Linguistic_Expression.notes: The Cyrillic alphabet contains 6 vowels and 29 consonants. The written language is based on the standard Tajik of the Republic.

Signed_Linguistic_Expression.definition: Not applicable. Tajik is primarily spoken and written; no signed variety is documented.

Linguistic_Property.definition: Properties that characterize linguistic units in Tajik.

Syntactic: Agreement (subject-verb agreement in person and number)

Linguistic_Data_Structure.definition: Abstract containers for grouping together instances of linguistic data.

structures.definition: Dictionary entry: хона 'house', китоб 'book', хондан 'to read'.
Set of forms for a verb in different tenses: хондам (I read), мехонам (I read, I am reading), хоҳам хонд (I will read).

Literary_Language.definition: The standard, codified form of Tajik used in official contexts and education.

variants.Codified: Used in official and prepared communication, based on northern dialects.
variants.Spoken: Used in informal communication, may include colloquialisms and dialectal features.

Non-literary_Varieties.Social_Dialects: Differences between urban and rural varieties; age-based variations.
Non-literary_Varieties.Vernacular: Colloquial speech, often characterized by reduced forms and borrowing from Uzbek and Russian.

Thing.definition: In KonabГЁre ontology, Thing is the superclass of all classes. All linguistic units are instances of Thing.

Abstract.definition: Grammatical categories in Tajik are abstract: number, tense, aspect, mood, case, definiteness.

Object.definition: Tajik nouns refer to objects: хона 'house' (physical object), одам 'man' (human), Душанбе 'city' (location).

Process.definition: Tajik verbs describe processes: рафтан 'to go', навиштан 'to write', хондан 'to read', зиндагӣ кардан 'to live'.

Phonetics.definition: The study of the sound system of Tajik.

sub-branches.Articulatory: Study of how Tajik speech sounds are produced (e.g., labial, dental, palatal, velar, uvular).
sub-branches.Acoustic: Study of acoustic properties of Tajik vowels and consonants.
sub-branches.Perceptual: Study of how Tajik sounds are perceived.

Linguistic_Phonetics.definition: Studies the function of sound means in Tajik, focusing on phonemes.
Linguistic_Phonetics.details: Tajik has 6 vowel and 24 consonant phonemes, with stress playing a significant functional role.

Phonetic_Units.definition: Linear objects in the speech chain.

types.name: Sound
types.definition: Concrete realization of a phoneme in a specific context.

types.name: Sound Type
types.definition: Abstract grouping of phonetically similar sounds.

types.name: Phoneme
types.definition: Abstract unit that distinguishes meaning (e.g., /p/ vs /b/ in 'пор' (piece) vs 'бор' (burden)).

Suprasegmental_Units.definition: Units consisting of segmental units organized into larger prosodic structures.

Segment_Features: Voicing (voiced vs voiceless: b/p, d/t, g/k, z/s, ʒ/ʃ, dʒ/tʃ, v/f)
Place of articulation (bilabial, labiodental, dental, alveolar, postalveolar, palatal, velar, uvular, glottal)
Manner of articulation (stop, fricative, affricate, nasal, lateral, tap/trill, approximant)
Suprasegmental_Features: Stress (dynamic, usually on the last syllable, but mobile with suffixes and in some word classes)
Intonation (rising for questions, falling for statements, and conveying various pragmatic meanings)

Phonetic_Rules.definition: Rules governing the use and variation of phonetic units.
Phonological_Rules: Vowel reduction in unstressed syllables (especially /a/ to [ə])
Consonant voicing assimilation (voiced consonants become voiceless before voiceless consonants, and vice versa)
Elision of certain consonants in clusters (e.g., /v/ in 'меравам' → 'мерам')
Assimilation of /n/ to a following labial consonant (e.g., 'шамбa' ← 'шанба')
Coarticulatory_Rules: Nasalization of vowels adjacent to nasal consonants
Elision of vowels in rapid speech

notes.ŋ: voiced velar nasal (occurs before /g/ and in some loanwords)

notes.ʔ: voiceless glottal stop (in loanwords from Arabic)

phonological_notes.voicing_assimilation: Voiced obstruents are devoiced in final position and before voiceless consonants: китоб [kiˈtop] 'book', дарс [dars] 'lesson'.
phonological_notes.q_χ_distribution: /q/ is often pronounced as [χ] in some dialects and in certain positions (e.g., бозор [boˈzoχ] 'bazaar').
phonological_notes.ɣ_dialect_variation: /ɣ/ is present in some dialects and in loanwords, but may be pronounced as [ʁ] or [g].

vowel_reduction.definition: Vowels are reduced in unstressed syllables. /a/ is often reduced to [ə] or [ʌ], /i/ and /u/ may be reduced to [ɪ] and [ʊ].

samarkand_bukhara.description: In the Samarkand and Bukhara dialects, the vowel /a/ is frequently fronted to [e] or [æ] in certain environments.

northern.description: In northern dialects, the vowel /a/ is typically pronounced as a low back vowel [ɑ], similar to the Russian 'a'.

Syllable.definition: In Tajik, syllables follow a structure of (C)(C)V(C)(C).

structures.V: Rare; occurs in some pronouns and conjunctions.

Stress.definition: Stress is usually on the last syllable of a word. Adding suffixes shifts stress to the new last syllable. In finite verb forms, stress is often on the first syllable, particularly with the prefix 'ме-'.
exceptions: Certain loanwords retain their original stress (e.g., 'кафедра' 'department').
The negation prefix 'на-' and the durative prefix 'ме-' take primary stress in finite verb forms.

Intonation.definition: Intonation is used to distinguish sentence types and convey pragmatic meaning.
functions: Falling intonation for statements and wh-questions.
Complex intonation patterns for expressing emotions and emphasis.

Phonological_System.definition: The phonological system of Tajik is based on a system of 6 vowels and 24 consonants, with vowel reduction, stress, and intonation playing a significant role.
Phonological_System.vowel_system: 6 vowels organized in a system with front/back, high/mid/low distinctions, and rounding.
Phonological_System.consonant_system: 24 consonants with contrasts in voicing, place, and manner, including uvular and glottal stops.

Orthographic_System.definition: Tajik has a standardized orthography based on the Cyrillic alphabet, adopted in 1940.
Orthographic_System.alphabet: 35 letters: А а, Б б, В в, Г г, Д д, Е е, Ё ё, Ж ж, З з, И и, Й й, К к, Қ қ, Л л, М м, Н н, О о, П п, Р р, С с, Т т, У у, Ф ф, Х х, Ҳ ҳ, Ч ч, Ҷ ҷ, Ш ш, Ъ ъ, Э э, Ю ю, Я я.

vowel_representation.oral: а, е, и, о, у, э
vowel_representation.notes: The vowel 'е' is used to represent /e/ and also for the 'yoted' vowels /je/ and /jo/ in initial and post-vocalic positions.

tonal_marking.notes: Tajik is not a tonal language. Stress is not marked orthographically in most cases.

Orthographic_System.punctuation: Uses standard Cyrillic punctuation marks (.,!?, etc.).

Morphology.definition: The branch of linguistics studying the internal structure of words, their forms, and the rules for combining meaningful units in Tajik. Tajik is a highly agglutinative-fusional language, using suffixation extensively for both inflection and derivation.
Morphology.key_focus: Identifying patterns of systematic covariation between form and meaning, particularly in agglutinative-fusional morphology, vowel harmony, and consonant alternations.

Goals.elegant_description: Capture generalizations about Tajik morphology, not just list facts.
Goals.cognitively_realistic_description: Reflect the mental grammar of Tajik speakers.
Goals.system_external_explanation: Link morphological patterns to factors outside the system, such as historical contact with Persian, Arabic, Russian, and Uzbek.

Word.definition: A complex concept with several distinct senses in Tajik.

Lexeme.definition: An abstract dictionary word representing a core meaning.

Word-form.definition: A concrete occurrence of a lexeme in speech.

Word_token.definition: A specific occurrence in a text.
Word_token.example: The token хона in the sentence 'Ман ба хона меравам'

Morpheme.definition: The smallest meaningful (sign) unit in Tajik. Cannot be divided into smaller meaningful parts.
Morpheme.key_properties: Cannot be divided into smaller meaningful parts.

Free.definition: Can stand alone as a word.

Bound.definition: Cannot stand alone, must attach to another morpheme.

Cumulation.definition: Expression of multiple meanings by a single marker.
types: Grammatical: past tense suffix -д expresses both past tense and perfective aspect
Lexical and Grammatical: personal suffixes on verbs express both person and number

Allomorphy.definition: Variation in form of a morpheme.
conditioning: Grammatical: different allomorphs for different cases (e.g., -ро, -а for the definite direct object)

deviations_from_additive_model.Fusion: Loss of clear boundary between morphemes in some contracted forms.

types_by_expression.Operational: Modification of another morpheme: vowel change in some irregular verbs
types_by_expression.Zero: Meaningful absence: nominative case has zero suffix

Morph.definition: A concrete, linear realization of a morpheme.

examples.-ҳо: allomorph of plural suffix after consonants and vowels
examples.-он: allomorph of plural suffix for animate nouns
examples.-ён: allomorph of plural suffix for nouns ending in a vowel

Affix.definition: A bound morpheme attaching to a base. Tajik uses almost exclusively suffixes, with some prefixes from Persian and Arabic.

Prefix.definition: Attach to beginning. Rare in native words, mostly from Persian and Arabic.

Suffix.definition: Attach to end. This is the primary morphological device in Tajik.

Root.definition: The base form of a word which cannot be further analyzed without total loss of identity.

Stem.definition: A root plus one or more derivational suffixes, to which inflectional suffixes are added.

Clitic.definition: A prosodically dependent unit with syntactic freedom.

Proclitic.definition: A clitic that precedes the lexical unit.

Enclitic.definition: A clitic that is phonologically joined at the end.

Compound.definition: A linguistic unit composed of elements that function independently.
Compound.structure: Two or more words combined; plural marked on the second element.

types.Endocentric: The compound is a hyponym of its head: сардар (a type of person with a head position)
types.Exocentric: The meaning is not derived from the parts: балогард 'catastrophe'

Inflection.definition: Morphological relationship between word-forms of a single lexeme.

key_properties: Less regular and productive than inflection

-чӣ.function: Forms agent nouns from verbs and nouns

-ӣ.function: Forms abstract nouns from adjectives and nouns, and adjectives from nouns

-гар.function: Forms agent nouns from verbs and nouns

-гон.function: Forms plural of some nouns, especially animate nouns

ме-.function: Forms durative aspect and present-future tense

ҳам-.function: Forms nouns and adjectives meaning 'co-, fellow, same'

Compounding.definition: Combination of two or more lexemes to form a new one.

types.Endocentric: One element is the head: сарвар 'leader' (сар 'head' + вар 'having')

examples.Noun+Noun: даступо 'hands and feet', сардӯш 'cover', хонабозор 'house market'

Morphological_Operations.Word_Formation: Cover term for derivation and compounding.

Lexicon.definition: The total store of words available to a speaker. Tajik lexicon contains a large number of native Iranian roots, with extensive borrowings from Arabic, Persian, Russian, Uzbek, and other languages.
Lexicon.notes: Tajik lexicon includes nouns, verbs, adjectives, adverbs, pronouns, postpositions, particles, numerals, and ideophones.

Lexical_Item.definition: A unit of the vocabulary. Includes native Iranian roots and numerous borrowings.

Inflectional_Paradigm.definition: The complete set of grammatical word-forms of a lexeme.
Inflectional_Paradigm.Inflection_Class: Group of lexemes sharing the same set of forms. Tajik has regular and irregular paradigms.
Inflectional_Paradigm.Syncretism: Two or more functions expressed by the same form.
Inflectional_Paradigm.Periphrasis: Use of a separate word or phrase.

Grammatical_Meaning.definition: Meanings obligatorily expressed by the grammar.
Grammatical_Meaning.Grammatical_Category: A set of mutually exclusive, obligatory meanings.
Grammatical_Meaning.Grammeme: An individual value within a category.

Agreement_Class_Gender.definition: Tajik does not have grammatical gender. Natural gender is expressed lexically or through compounding (e.g., писари 'boy' vs духтар 'girl').

Case.definition: Marks syntactic and/or semantic role through suffixes and postpositions. There are five main cases in Tajik.

Accusative/Dative.function: Definite direct object, indirect object with certain verbs

plural_suffix.rule: The most common plural suffix is -ҳо, which is added to all nouns. -он (and its variants -ён, -гон) is used for animate nouns and some inanimate nouns.

special_cases.pluralia_tantum: Words with only plural form: шим 'pants', айнок 'glasses'
special_cases.mass_nouns: Do not take plural when used generically: об 'water', нон 'bread'

referential_usage.Definite: Marked by the direct object marker -ро for definite direct objects
referential_usage.Indefinite: Marked by the indefinite marker -е or by the numeral як 'one'

non-referential_usage.Generic: Unmarked noun: Шир хуб аст. 'Milk is good.'

Possession.definition: Possession is expressed through the izafet construction (possessor follows the possessed noun with the izafet marker -и) or through possessive suffixes.

Aspect.definition: Presents situation from internal temporal perspective.

core_meanings.Perfective: Action viewed as a whole (usually past tense)
core_meanings.Imperfective: Action viewed as ongoing (present tense, progressive)

subtypes: Iterative (repeated on one occasion with гирифтан)

Tense.definition: Locates event relative to moment of speech.

core_meanings.Future: хоҳам + infinitive or me- + present stem

Pluperfect.suffix: past stem + -а + будам, будӣ, буд, будем, будед, буданд

negation_suffix.position: Before the verb stem or the ме- prefix

subtypes.Active: Default voice. The subject performs the action.

Causative.example: хондан 'to read' → хондан 'to make someone read'

Inflection_vs_Derivation_Criteria: Relevance to syntax: Inflection is more relevant
Regularity and productivity: Inflection is more regular
Meaning compositionality: Inflection is more compositional
Word class change: Derivation can change class
Position relative to base: Derivation is closer to root

processes: Assimilation of /n/ to a following labial

Syntax-Morphology_Interface.lexical_integrity: Syntactic rules cannot access internal morphological structure.

Morphology_and_Other_Components.Morphology_and_Valence: How morphology affects argument structure: causative adds an agent, passive removes an agent.

Productivity.definition: Ability to apply to new bases.
restrictions: Semantic: some derivational suffixes only apply to certain semantic classes
Pragmatic: some strategies are less productive
Morphological: borrowed vocabulary may not follow native patterns
Productivity.blocking: Existing word prevents formation of a potential synonym.

key_patterns: Common values are shorter (e.g., -д for past tense)
High frequency forms are irregular (e.g., будан 'to be' has irregular forms)

Morphological_Typology.Degree_of_Synthesis: High morpheme-per-word ratio; complex suffixation and compounding.

Part_Of_Speech_Property.definition: The property that identifies the grammatical class of a word.

classes.Noun: Names of entities; take plural, case, and possessive markers
classes.Verb: Actions and states; show TAM distinctions
classes.Adjective: Quality words; can be used as nouns
classes.Adverb: Modify verbs; often derived from adjectives with -ӣ
classes.Postposition: Follow nouns; mark spatial, instrumental, and beneficiary relations

Particles.definition: Invariable grammatical items that serve various functions, including negation, interrogation, and discourse marking.

-мӣ.position: Enclitic to the verb or the word being questioned

-да.function: Particle indicating confirmation or emphasis (tag question equivalent)
-да.position: Enclitic, often at the end of a clause

ки.function: Subordinating conjunction (that, because), also used as a relative pronoun
ки.position: At the beginning of a subordinate clause

ҳам.position: Enclitic to the word it modifies

-е.position: Enclitic to the noun or adjective

магар.function: Particle expressing doubt, surprise, or contrast (often 'but' or 'surely')
магар.position: At the beginning of a clause

балки.function: Particle meaning 'but, rather, on the contrary'
балки.position: At the beginning of a clause

examples.sentence: На ба хона, балки ба кор рафт.
examples.translation: He didn't go home, but to work.

Bound_Morpheme.examples: Plural suffix -ҳо, past tense -д, infinitives -ан, agentive -чӣ

Inflectional_Morpheme.definition: Express grammatical categories; do not change word class.
Inflectional_Morpheme.examples: Plural suffix -ҳо, case suffixes, tense suffixes

Derivational_Morpheme.definition: Derive new lexical units; may change word class.

Suffix.examples: All primary inflectional and derivational morphemes

Category_Changer.definition: Derivational units that change the syntactic category of the root.

Nominalizer.definition: Forms a noun from some other word class.

Intransitivizer.definition: Derives an intransitive verb from a transitive verb.
Intransitivizer.examples: Passive voice: навиштан 'to write' → навишта шудан 'to be written'

Transitivizer.definition: Derives transitive verbs from intransitive verb stems.
Transitivizer.examples: Causative: хондан 'to read' → хондан 'to make someone read'

Copula.definition: Indicates a relationship of equivalency between subject and predicate.

Auxiliary.definition: Verbs used in coordination with another verb to express mood, tense or aspect.

Modal.definition: Expresses necessity, possibility, attitude toward factuality.

Negation_Operator.examples: на- (verbal negation), не (nominal negation), нест (existential negation)

Personal_Pronoun.definition: Refers to speaker, addressee, and others.

Demonstrative.definition: Used deictically to indicate spatial, temporal, or discourse location.

Quantifier.definition: Expresses definite or indefinite number or amount.

ordinal.formation: Ordinal numerals are formed by adding the suffix -ум (or -ом after vowels) to the cardinal numeral: як → якум (first), ду → дувум (second), се → сеюм (third), чор → чорум (fourth).

Ergativity.definition: Tajik exhibits an ergative construction in the past tense of transitive verbs. In this construction, the subject of a transitive verb takes the oblique (genitive) case, while the object takes the nominative case. The verb agrees with the object in person and number, not the subject.
Ergativity.historical_context: This ergative pattern is a retention from Middle Persian, which had a similar construction. It distinguishes Tajik from other Persian dialects, which have largely lost this feature.

examples.analysis: ман (I) is the subject in the ergative case, китобро (the book) is the object in the accusative, and хондам (I read) agrees with the subject.
ӯ (he) is the subject in the ergative case, китобро (the book) is the object, and хонд (read) agrees with the object (3SG).
мо (we) is the subject in the ergative case, китобро (the book) is the object, and хондем (read) agrees with the subject (1PL).
The intransitive verb agrees with the subject in the nominative case.

Ergativity.notes: The ergative construction is a significant feature of Tajik, distinguishing it from Persian. It is thought to be a result of contact with Turkic languages or a retention from Old Iranian.

Generative_Grammar.definition: Grammar viewed as a cognitive faculty; language generated by a set of rules.

key_assumptions.I-Language: Internal, psychological, cognitive system of grammatical knowledge
key_assumptions.E-Language: External, physical, social manifestation of language
key_assumptions.Performance: Actual use of language, subject to external factors

Basic_Word_Order.definition: SOV (Subject-Object-Verb) order is standard in Tajik, though it can be flexible due to topicalization.
Basic_Word_Order.example: Ман китобро мехонам. 'I am reading the book.'

variations.OSV: For emphasis: Китобро ман мехонам. 'It is I who is reading the book.'
variations.VSO: Rare, in some questions or poetic contexts: Мехонам ман китобро? 'Am I reading the book?'

Interrogative_Word_Order.definition: In interrogative sentences, the word order typically remains SOV, but the question particle or interrogative word may be fronted for emphasis.

yes_no_questions.structure: Rising intonation or the question particle -мӣ is suffixed to the verb or a prominent word in the sentence.

wh_questions.structure: The wh-word (кӣ, чӣ, куҷо, etc.) remains in the position of the constituent it replaces, though it may be fronted for focus.

examples.translation: Whom do you see? (focus on object)

Postpositions.definition: Function words that follow nouns to indicate case relations.

examples.negative: мӯаллим нестам 'I am not a teacher'

yes_no.alternative: Rising intonation in colloquial speech: Гуфтед? 'Did you say?'

Theta_Roles.Theta_Criterion: Each argument assigned one and only one theta role; each theta role assigned to one argument.

Constituents.definition: A group of words functioning as a single unit.

examples.phrase: китобро мехонам 'I am reading the book'

examples: аз хона калонтар 'bigger than the house'

Clause_Structure.example: Ман китобро мехонам. 'I am reading the book.'

Interrogative.content: Ту кадом китобро мехонӣ? 'Which book are you reading?'

Conditional.example: Агар меомадӣ, ман низ меомадам. 'If you came, I would come too.'

examples.clause: омада одам 'the man who is coming'
хонда китоб 'the book that was read'

Theme_and_Rheme.Theme: Starting point, what sentence is about.
Theme_and_Rheme.Rheme: New information, what is said about theme.

Communicative_Categories.Topic: Grammaticalized theme, often marked by position at the beginning of sentence.
Communicative_Categories.Focus: Most salient, emphasized part; often fronted.
Communicative_Categories.Given_vs_New: Information assumed known vs. newly introduced.

Agreement.definition: Subject-verb agreement in person and number.
Agreement.example: Ман меравам 'I go', Ту меравӣ 'You go'

Government.definition: Postpositions determine case marking of noun phrases.

Adjunct.definition: A phrase modifying a head but not an actant.

Syntactic_Relations.Apposition: Two noun phrases juxtaposed referring to the same entity.
Syntactic_Relations.example: Надир, дӯсти ман, дар ин ҷо зиндагӣ мекунад. 'Nadir, my friend, lives here.'

Semantics.definition: The branch of linguistics studying meaning in Tajik.

Truth-Conditional_Semantics.definition: To know meaning is to know truth-conditions.

Compositionality.definition: Meaning of complex expression determined by meanings of parts and combination rules.

Lexical_Meaning.definition: Meaning of a word as a unit of the lexicon.

components.Pragmatic_Component: Conditions of use and speaker's attitude

Polysemy.definition: Single word with multiple related meanings.
Polysemy.example: даст 'hand' also means 'help, assistance' (даст расондан 'to help')

from_Arabic.description: Arabic loanwords are primarily found in religious, legal, and scientific terminology. They often retain Arabic broken plurals and specific phonological features.

from_Persian.description: Persian loanwords form a large part of the Tajik vocabulary, especially in the domains of culture, art, and everyday life. Many of these words are shared with Farsi.

from_Russian.description: Russian loanwords are particularly common in technical, administrative, and Soviet-era terminology. They often refer to modern concepts and inventions, and many have been nativized in pronunciation and morphology.
reasons_for_extensive_borrowing: Soviet rule (1920-1991) established Russian as the dominant language of administration, science, and technology.
Russian was the language of higher education and technical professions.
Many modern concepts and inventions were introduced through Russian.
Russian words often had no equivalent in Tajik at the time of borrowing.

from_Uzbek.description: Uzbek loanwords are common in the southern dialects (Samarkand, Bukhara) due to extensive bilingualism and cultural contact. They often relate to everyday life, agriculture, and commerce.

Grammatical_Meaning.definition: Abstract, obligatory, systematic meaning expressed by grammatical markers.
key_categories: Tense (past -д, present-future ме-, future хоҳам + infinitive)

Propositional_Component.Proposition: Set of possible worlds or truth-value.
Propositional_Component.Argument_Structure: List of participants with semantic roles.

Communicative_Component.Given_New: Information assumed known vs. newly introduced.

Pragmatic_Component.definition: Information about speaker's intention and use.
Pragmatic_Component.Illocutionary_Force: Type of act (assertion, question, command, wish)

Referential_Status.Definite: Marked by -ро for direct objects or implied by context
Referential_Status.Generic: Unmarked: Китоб фоида дорад. 'Books are useful.'

ordinal.formation: Ordinal numerals are formed by adding the suffix -ум (or -ом after vowels) to the cardinal numeral: як → якум (first), ду → дувум (second), се → сеюм (third), чор → чорум (fourth).

compound_numerals.structure: Compound numerals are formed by connecting the tens and units with the conjunction 'у' (and). For example: бисту як (21), бисту ду (22), сӣ (30), чилу панҷ (45), панҷоҳу шаш (56).

Phonetics-Phonology_Interface.definition: The interaction between the substance of speech and its functional organization.
key_areas: Phonological rules: vowel reduction, consonant voicing assimilation
Phonetic transcription: Mapping from phonemes to phonetic realization

Phonology-Morphology_Interface.definition: The interaction between sound structure and word structure.
key_areas: Vowel reduction in unstressed syllables in suffixes
Consonant alternations (voicing assimilation, elision in clusters)
Stress patterns in word formation and inflection

Morphology-Syntax_Interface.definition: The interaction between word structure and sentence structure.
key_areas: Lexical Integrity: Syntactic rules cannot access internal morphological structure
Agreement: Subject-verb agreement in person and number
Case assignment: Postpositions and prepositions assign case to noun phrases
Valence changing operations: Causative -он- adds an agent, passive -шудан removes an agent

Syntax-Semantics_Interface.definition: The interaction between sentence structure and meaning.
key_areas: Compositionality: Meaning derived from parts and their combination
TAM marking: Tense, aspect, mood express temporal and modal meaning
Conditional constructions: -а + ли for real conditions

Semantics-Pragmatics_Interface.definition: The interaction between literal meaning and context-dependent interpretation.
key_areas: Speech acts: Declaratives, interrogatives, imperatives, wishes
Presupposition: Background information in relative clauses
Definiteness and reference: Marked by -ро or implied by context
Focus and topicalization: Fronting for information structure

subject.definition: Agent of transitive verb or single argument of intransitive verb.

agent.definition: Semantic role of the doer of the action.

patient.definition: Semantic role of the undergoer of the action.

allomorph.definition: Relation between a morpheme and its allomorphs.

allophone.definition: Relation between a phoneme and its phones.

realization.definition: Relation between a linguistic unit and its physical form.

semanticRole.definition: Relation between a participant and a predicate.

argument.definition: The syntactic entity about which something is predicated.

inLanguage.definition: Relation between a linguistic sign and Tajik.

phoneticRep.definition: Phonetic representation of a linguistic unit.

phonemicRep.definition: Phonemic representation of a linguistic unit.

orthographicRep.definition: Orthographic representation of a linguistic unit.

gloss.definition: Gloss or translation of a linguistic unit.

hasExample.definition: Example usage of a linguistic unit.

stringRep.definition: String representation of a linguistic unit.

Lexicon_Overview.definition: The lexicon of Tajik includes a large number of native Iranian roots, with extensive borrowings from Arabic, Persian, Russian, Uzbek, and other languages. The lexicon is characterized by a high degree of derivational morphology, with a variety of suffixes for forming new words.
Lexicon_Overview.word_structure: Most words are disyllabic or monosyllabic; CV and CVC syllable structures most common.
Lexicon_Overview.loanwords: Primarily from Arabic, Persian, Russian, and Uzbek; adapt to native phonotactic constraints.
Lexicon_Overview.noun_classes: Nouns are not classified by grammatical gender. Natural gender is expressed lexically.
Lexicon_Overview.nominal_compounds: Highly productive; plural marked on the second constituent.

idiomatic_expressions.definition: Idiomatic expressions are fixed phrases whose meaning is not predictable from the meanings of their individual components. They are common in Tajik and often have cultural or metaphorical origins.

examples.meaning: to start working, get down to business
to fall in love, to be captivated
to take seriously, to be strict
addicted to something, fond of something
